correctness.rationale: The vertex sets, edge sets, and triangle-avoidance faces are explicitly normalized. Separate exhaustive predicates agree for every one of 2^16 subsets. The Shrikhande complex has 8,951 faces including empty, 4,471 matching pairs and exactly nine critical dimension-six simplices; the rook complex has 7,343 faces, 3,664 pairs and fifteen critical dimension-five simplices. Both augmented matchings pair empty with a singleton. Every oriented codimension-one Hasse incidence (48,288 Shrikhande; 37,744 rook) was included in a completed acyclic topological sort. Removing the empty pairing leaves a standard acyclic matching with one critical vertex and only top-dimensional positive critical cells, proving both integral wedge homotopy types by Forman. Independent complete mod-two simplicial boundary reductions return Betti 9 in degree 6 and Betti 15 in degree 5; these are corroboration only. All computations are replayed in the included standalone program.

originality.rationale: The rook equivalence M_2(K_{4,4}) ~ wedge of fifteen 5-spheres is already established (published-finding corpus 915eed6b65e5) and is not asserted new. The new claim is the exact integral Shrikhande triangle-avoidance homotopy wedge of nine 6-spheres, leading to a dimensional separation between two strongly regular graphs with the same 32 triangles. Direct inspected papers on devoid complexes and generalized chessboard complexes do not cover Shrikhande, and related indexed Shrikhande topology records use different complexes. Lack of a discovered equivalent cannot establish absolute novelty; unindexed coverage remains a real risk.
residual_risks: Equivalent unpublished, unindexed, or differently named computation of the Shrikhande triangle hypergraph independence complex may exist.

value.rationale: The Shrikhande graph is the unique exceptional strongly regular counterpart of the four-by-four rook graph with parameters (16,6,2,2). The 32 triangles of Shrikhande encode a natural toroidal triangulation, so excluding complete triangular faces is an intrinsic invariant, not an arbitrary slice. The integral wedge-of-nine-six-spheres classification is a complete answer for this canonical object and changes the degree of its only homology relative to the already known rook case. Therefore graph parameters and triangle counts do not determine this triangle-avoidance homotopy invariant. This structural distinction is meaningful independently of whether a broad family theorem exists.
